subject: Tortoise Bank — throughput stall & sustained error bursts (reserved capacity shortfall)
messages:
From: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@tortoisebank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Ng <claire.ng@tortoisebank.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate: production throughput collapse + 500s on dedicated pool

Team,

We just hit a hard drop in production throughput and are seeing sustained 500s and timeouts from the Redwood endpoint serving our fraud-detection model. Throughput fell from ~1.2k req/s to ~180 req/s over the last 30m and latency p99 jumped from ~120ms to >2.4s. This is on our reserved/dedicated pool (reservation ID R-7721) — we expected reserved capacity to prevent this class of outage.

Attached are a short snippet of logs and a screenshot of our internal dashboard. This is directly impacting authorizations; our ops team has started rolling back traffic to a degraded rule set.

Please advise: is this a capacity enforcement issue on your side, or are we mis-configured? We need an ETA for stabilization and a statement on guarantees — we have an upcoming renewal discussion next week and this is material.

Attaching: tortoise_error_snippets.log (6KB)

Ethan
Ethan Shaw
Head of Platform Engineering — Tortoise Bank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@tortoisebank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: production throughput collapse + 500s on dedicated pool

Ethan — thanks for the alert and the logs. We’re on a triage bridge now (joining Claire shortly). Initial triage steps:

- Confirming whether reservation R-7721 is being honored at the scheduler layer.
- Pulling pool metrics (GPU utilization, queue depth, inflight tokens) for the last 90 minutes.
- Checking for large-context or long-running requests that can monopolize slots.

Plan: Jonas and Olga are running the first-pass diagnostics. I will coordinate a short customer-facing status update in 20–30 minutes and propose mitigation steps. We’ll also collect a timeline and attach evidence for postmortem.

We understand the impact given your upcoming renewal and will prioritize.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: ACTION: urgent exec-level escalation if reserved capacity not restored in 2h — Tortoise Bank (R-7721)

Team —

Customer: Tortoise Bank (DB-4729). Impact: production authorization failures; customer rolled back to fallback rules. This is high priority for commercial and retention reasons — renewal call next week.

If we cannot restore their reserved throughput within 2 hours, escalate to execs (myself + sales leadership + CTO). Immediate asks:

1) Confirm whether reservation R-7721 is being enforced at the orchestration/ticketing layer or if reservation drift is occurring.
2) If enforcement has failed, perform a temporary isolation of the dedicated pool (evict non-reserved workloads) and reassign sufficient GPU capacity to meet the baseline of 1.2k req/s.
3) Provide a short-term mitigation plan (15–60m horizon) and a durable plan for preventing recurrence (tenant hard-isolation / stronger admission controls).
4) Prepare a customer-facing timeline and credit/SL mitigation proposal for my review.

Goal: demonstrate we have root cause and a concrete timeline before we loop the CEO/CTO. If we can resolve within the window, we keep this with engineering/SE + account team. If not, I need a one-page exec brief within 45 minutes to decide escalation.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACTION: urgent exec-level escalation if reserved capacity not restored in 2h — Tortoise Bank (R-7721)

Quick technical findings from the triage bridge:

- Symptom: sustained GPU saturation on pool dp-auk-14 serving multiple tenants. Observed long-tail requests (context lengths ~12k tokens) causing KV-cache pressure and effective slot starvation.
- Reservation metric: there is evidence of reservation drift — scheduler allowed best-effort jobs to consume headroom when the pool was under transient pressure. Reserve usage snapshot attached.

Short-term mitigations (immediate):
- Isolate dp-auk-14 from best-effort routing and force schedule only reserved tenants (we can do this now).
- Evict long-running best-effort requests by marking active requests for graceful preemption (5–10s drain).
- If isolation is insufficient, temporarily scale a fallback dedicated unit (hot spare) and warm it with the same model quantization.

Longer-term (post-incident):
- Harden reservation enforcement path and add strict admission-control gates to prevent drift.
- Add alerting on reservation drift + long-request token distribution signatures.

Attachments: reserve_usage_snapshot.csv, throughput_chart_aug20-22.png

I’ll start isolation now and report back in 12 minutes with the effect on throughput.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@tortoisebank.com>
Cc: Claire Ng <claire.ng@tortoisebank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: production throughput collapse + 500s on dedicated pool

Ethan — quick status update from our side and an ask.

What we’ve done so far:
- Isolated the dedicated pool to deny best-effort routing; evicted non-reserved long-running requests.
- Warmed a hot-spare GPU shard and rebalanced R-7721 traffic across both units; observed preliminary throughput recovery to ~920 req/s and latency p95 back down to ~200–300ms.

Ask for you: please confirm the business-safe rollback threshold (requests/sec or successful authorizations/min) we should target for the next 3 hours so we can route traffic conservatively while we finish hardening. Also confirm whether you want an exec-level call in the next 60 minutes — Marcus may request escalation if we do not hit 1.2k req/s.

We will follow up with a post-incident summary and proposed SLA credit. Appreciate the logs you sent — those helped identify the long-context request pattern.

Attachments: tortoise_error_snippets.log (copied to incident bundle)

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: CEO <ceo@redwood.com>, CTO <cto@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Exec note: Tortoise Bank incident recap + decision request (R-7721)

Folks —

High-level: Tortoise Bank (DB-4729) experienced reserved-capacity throughput shortfall on 2027-08-20 due to reservation enforcement drift combined with multi-tenant long-context requests. Engineering performed pool isolation and temporary scaling; customer recovered to ~920 req/s within 30m but remains below their contracted baseline (1.2k req/s) while we harden the control plane.

Commercial ask: approve a 30-day SLA exception and one month of service credit (pro-rated) while we complete enforcement fixes. Engineering asks: approval to prioritize a capacity purchase (hot spare units) and a schedule to deliver reservation enforcement patches within 10 business days.

Decision needed (reply-all):
- Approve SLA exception + one-month pro-rated credit to Tortoise Bank? (yes/no)
- Approve immediate budget to warm/assign a hot-spare dedicated unit for high-risk reserved customers? (yes/no)

Background docs + incident artifacts: https://hubspot.example/deal/DB-4729 | https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Tortoise-Thruput-Analysis

I recommend approval on both to contain commercial risk; if approved I will coordinate the customer exec call and the credit communication.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
